mainTopic: Roasting the קרבן פסח: the pomegranate spit, metal vs. wood, the גדי מקולס today, and רבה's rule of כבולעו כך פולטו for stuffed meat
overview: The משנה teaches that the פסח is roasted on a pomegranate-wood spit pushed through the whole animal. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the legs and innards go inside it, while רבי עקיבא says that is a kind of בישול and they must hang outside. The משנה also bans a metal spit or grill, and רבי צדוק tells a story about רבן גמליאל roasting on an אסכלא. The גמרא explains why only pomegranate wood works. Metal heats through and roasts the meat by itself, not by fire (צלי אש). Palm, fig, oak, carob and sycamore all release liquid and make the meat like מבושל. It then notes that רבי יהודה allows a metal spit, but the חכמים answer that metal heats all the way through while wood does not. Next, a ברייתא gives nicknames for the roasted פסח and defines the גדי מקולס that may not be eaten on פסח night today, with רב ששת clarifying the case of a boiled limb. Finally, רבה permits roasting meat stuffed with unsalted meat because כבולעו כך פולטו. The גמרא tries to prove this from our משנה, but rejects the proof because of the open slaughter cut, and that reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How to roast the פסח: a pomegranate spit through the whole animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the roasting method. A pomegranate-wood שפוד goes from the mouth to the rear opening, and according to רבי יוסי הגלילי the legs and innards are placed inside the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How do we roast the פסח? We bring a spit of pomegranate wood and push it into the animal's mouth all the way through to its rear opening. Then we put its legs and innards inside it. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the topic by explaining exactly how the פסח is put on the spit and roasted. It also gives רבי יוסי הגלילי's view that the legs and innards are roasted inside the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah requires the פסח to be roasted, not cooked. The משנה specifies pomegranate wood, and the גמרא will soon explain why. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that putting the legs and innards inside the animal still counts as roasting.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: How does one roast the Paschal lamb?
One brings a spit of pomegranate wood,
and thrusts it into its mouth
until its rear opening,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹתֵן אֶת כְּרָעָיו וְאֶת בְּנֵי מֵעָיו לְתוֹכוֹ,
phrases.english: and places its legs and its entrails inside it,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסח is roasted on a pomegranate-wood spit running from mouth to rear; according to רבי יוסי הגלילי the legs and innards are placed inside it.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: putting the parts inside is like cooking
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. Placing the legs and innards inside the body is a form of בישול, so they must be hung outside the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: That is a kind of cooking! Rather, we hang them outside the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא argues with רבי יוסי הגלילי. He says the legs and innards must hang outside the body, not be stuffed inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Parts sealed inside the body are not touched directly by the fire. They cook in the steam and juices of the animal instead. That is closer to בישול, which is forbidden for the פסח, than to צלי אש, which the Torah requires.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main idea of the whole סוגיא: the פסח must be roasted directly by fire, and anything that makes it 'cooked' disqualifies it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
This is a type of cooking,
rather, one suspends them outside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּמִין בִּישּׁוּל הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling about the legs and innards
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The legs and innards are hung outside the animal, because placing them inside counts as a form of בישול.

steps.title: No roasting on a metal spit or a grill
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the פסח may not be roasted on a metal שפוד or on an אסכלא, a grill.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may not roast the פסח on a metal spit or on a grill.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new rule: certain tools may not be used to roast the פסח. These are a metal spit and a metal grill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hot metal roasts the meat by its own heat, not by the fire itself. The גמרא will soon explain this reasoning when it asks why a metal spit cannot be used.

phrases.english: One may not roast the Paschal lamb
neither on the metal spit
nor on the grill.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין צוֹלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח לֹא עַל הַשַּׁפּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new prohibition about roasting tools
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסח may not be roasted on a metal spit or a metal grill.

steps.title: The story of רבן גמליאל and his servant טבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק reports that רבן גמליאל told his servant טבי to roast the פסח on an אסכלא, which seems to contradict the rule just stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי צדוק said: There was an incident with רבן גמליאל, who said to his servant טבי: Go and roast the פסח for us on the grill.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a story that seems to allow a grill. That appears to clash with the rule right before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מעשה is brought as evidence of how a great sage actually acted. The tension between this story and the ban on an אסכלא is left open here. The גמרא will deal with it later in the סוגיא.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story brought as evidence
Tavi, his servant (רבן גמליאל's well-known servant)

steps.confusionAlert: This story does not cancel the rule just before it. The גמרא later explains what kind of grill רבן גמליאל used. Do not assume an ordinary grill is allowed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tzadok said:
There was an incident with Rabban Gamliel
who said to his servant Tavi:

phrases.aramaic: צֵא וּצְלֵה לָנוּ אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הָאַסְכָּלָא.
phrases.english: Go and roast the Paschal lamb for us on the grill.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי צָדוֹק: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that seems to be in tension with the ban on a grill
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל had the פסח roasted on an אסכלא, which needs to be reconciled with the prohibition.

steps.title: Why not use a metal spit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה requires a wooden spit. Why not simply use one made of metal?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Let them bring a metal spit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins asking why the משנה insists on pomegranate wood. It starts with the obvious choice, metal, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Metal does not drip water or sap, so it might seem like the cleanest option. The question forces the גמרא to explain what is wrong with metal.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: Let them bring a metal spit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins analyzing why the משנה requires pomegranate wood
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a metal spit is not acceptable

steps.title: Metal heats up and roasts the meat itself
steps.stepSummary: Once part of a metal spit is hot, the whole spit is hot. The meat would then be roasted by the spit, but the Torah requires צלי אש, roasting by fire and not by anything else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since when part of it is hot, all of it is hot, the meat gets roasted because of the spit. But the Merciful One said 'roasted in fire,' and not roasted because of something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that metal is not allowed. A hot metal spit would roast the meat from the inside instead of the fire doing the roasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words צלי אש teach that the fire itself must roast the פסח. Metal conducts heat, so the meat touching the spit is roasted by the spit. This also explains the משנה's ban on a metal spit and grill.
steps.whyThisMatters: צלי אש, roasting by fire alone, is the rule behind every answer that follows in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: Since when part of it is hot, all of it is hot,
and it gets roasted because of the spit,
and the Merciful One said: 'Roasted in fire,'
and not roasted because of something else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about metal
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Metal heats throughout and roasts the meat itself, which violates צלי אש.

steps.title: Why not palm wood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a wooden spit made from a palm tree instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them bring a spit of palm wood!
steps.whatsHappening: Metal has been ruled out, so the גמרא now asks why not use a different kind of wood, starting with palm. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood does not conduct heat the way metal does. The question is why the משנה specifically requires pomegranate and not any other wood.

phrases.english: Let them bring one of palm wood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from metal to another kind of wood
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a palm-wood spit is not acceptable

steps.title: Palm wood releases water
steps.stepSummary: Palm has grooves that release liquid during roasting, so the meat becomes like מבושל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it has grooves, it gives off water, and the meat becomes like cooked meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects palm wood. Liquid from its grooves would partly 'cook' the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new problem, separate from metal's. Here the issue is moisture: meat that sits in liquid while heating counts as cooked, not roasted.

phrases.english: Since it has grooves,
it gives off water
and it is like cooked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the palm question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Palm releases water from its grooves, making the meat like מבושל.

steps.title: Why not fig wood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests fig wood instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them bring a spit of fig wood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another wood, the fig tree. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fig wood does not have palm's grooves, so the palm problem might not apply to it.

phrases.english: Let them bring one of fig wood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes another wood after palm was rejected
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a fig-wood spit is not acceptable

steps.title: Fig wood is hollow and releases water
steps.stepSummary: Fig wood is hollow and full of sap, so it releases liquid and the meat becomes like מבושל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is hollow, it gives off water, and the meat becomes like cooked meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects fig wood for the same basic reason as palm: it releases liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source of the liquid is different. In palm it comes from grooves, and in fig it comes from the hollow, sappy inside. The result is the same, and the meat counts as cooked.

phrases.english: Since it is hollow,
it gives off water
and it is as though it is cooked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the fig question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Fig is hollow and releases water, making the meat like מבושל.

steps.title: Why not oak, carob, or sycamore?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests hard, dry woods with no sap: oak, carob, or sycamore.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them bring a spit of oak, of carob, or of sycamore!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes three hard woods that are neither grooved nor hollow. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These woods seem to avoid both earlier problems. So why not use them?

phrases.english: Let them bring one of oak,
of carob, or of sycamore?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנַיְתֵי שֶׁל אַלּוֹן, שֶׁל חָרוּב, וְשֶׁל שִׁקְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes harder woods that avoid the earlier problems
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why oak, carob, or sycamore spits are not acceptable

steps.title: These woods have knots that release water
steps.stepSummary: These trees have knots. They must be cut off to smooth the stick, and the cut spots release liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they have knots, they give off water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects these woods too. Their knots would leak liquid into the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hard wood has knots that must be shaved off to make a smooth spit. The fresh cuts release moisture, which brings back the problem of the meat becoming like מבושל.

phrases.english: Since it has knots,
it gives off water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the oak, carob and sycamore question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their knots, once cut, release water.

steps.title: But pomegranate also has knots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: pomegranate wood also has knots, so it should have the same problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pomegranate branch also has knots!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the reasoning against the משנה's own choice. If knots disqualify a spit, pomegranate should be disqualified too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The knot reasoning seems to prove too much. If it holds, the משנה's required wood would be just as unfit as the others.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל רִמּוֹן נָמֵי אִית בֵּיהּ קִיטְרֵי?
phrases.english: A pomegranate branch also has knots?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁל רִמּוֹן נָמֵי אִית בֵּיהּ קִיטְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the knot reasoning from the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement of pomegranate wood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If knots disqualify a spit, pomegranate wood, which also has knots, should be disqualified too.

steps.title: Pomegranate knots are smooth
steps.stepSummary: Pomegranate knots are smooth, so they do not need to be cut and do not release water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its knots are smooth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that pomegranate knots are different. They are smooth and need no cutting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real problem was never the knots themselves but the cutting, which opens the wood and lets liquid out. Pomegranate knots stay uncut, so no water comes out.

phrases.english: Its knots are smooth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the knot challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: pomegranate knots differ in kind
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All knots require cutting and leak water
steps.terutzMaskana: Pomegranate knots are smooth, need no cutting, and release no water

steps.title: A one-year-old branch has no knots
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the משנה refers to a young pomegranate branch in its first year, which has no knots at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: it refers to a one-year-old branch, which has no knots.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to answer the knot challenge. A first-year branch has no knots at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer accepted that pomegranate has knots and showed they are harmless. This answer avoids the knots entirely by limiting the משנה to a young branch.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
it refers to a branch within its first year,
which has no knots.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific type of branch
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a first-year branch with no knots at all

steps.title: But the cut end will release water
steps.stepSummary: Even a young branch has a spot where it was cut from the tree, and water could come out of that spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the place where it was cut!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the young-branch answer. Every branch has a cut end that could leak liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the knots does not solve everything. Cutting the branch off the tree leaves an open end, which brings back the water problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where it was cut

phrases.english: But there is the place where it was cut!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the young-branch answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a first-year branch has no knots
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every branch has a cut end where it was taken from the tree, and water could come out of it.

steps.title: The cut end sticks out of the animal
steps.stepSummary: The cut end is left sticking out of the animal, so any liquid from it never touches the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: One leaves the cut end outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the spit is placed so the cut end stays outside the body. Any water from it does not affect the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is only liquid inside the meat. Placing the spit so the cut end sticks out solves it completely, and pomegranate wood stays fit.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסח must be roasted by fire alone (צלי אש). Metal is out because it roasts with its own heat. Palm, fig, oak, carob and sycamore are out because they release liquid and make the meat like מבושל. Pomegranate is fit because its knots are smooth (or the branch is young and has none), and the cut end stays outside the animal.

phrases.english: That one places the cut end outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the cut-end challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cut end releases water into the meat
steps.terutzMaskana: The cut end is kept outside the animal, so no liquid reaches the meat

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה on the metal spit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה's ban on a metal spit is not the view of רבי יהודה. He holds that a metal spit, like a wooden one, does not get hot enough inside the animal to cook it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה. As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, just as a wooden spit does not burn, a metal spit does not become burning hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that someone disagrees with our משנה's rule against roasting the פסח on a metal spit. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says a metal spit is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's worry is that a hot metal spit would cook the meat from the inside, so the meat is not roasted by fire alone. רבי יהודה rejects this worry with a comparison. The part of a wooden spit inside the animal does not catch fire, so the part of a metal spit inside the animal also does not get hot enough to cook.

keyTerms.meaning: A spit, the rod used to hold meat over a fire
Just as... so too (introduces a comparison)

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.
As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Just as a spit of wood
phrases.notes: Meaning the part of the spit that is inside the animal.

phrases.english: does not burn,
so too a spit of metal
does not become burning hot.
phrases.notes: So it will not cook the meat from inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the pomegranate-wood discussion and returns to the משנה's rule against a metal spit, noting a dissenting תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a metal spit is allowed because the part inside the animal does not get hot enough to cook the meat, just as the wood inside does not burn.

steps.title: The Sages reject the comparison: metal heats all the way through
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה that metal and wood are different. Heat one part of metal and all of it gets hot. Heat one part of wood and the rest stays cool.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: With this one (metal), when part of it is hot, all of it is hot. With that one (wood), when part of it is hot, not all of it is hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue against רבי יהודה's comparison between wood and metal. They point to a real physical difference between the two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's argument works only if wood and metal behave the same way. The חכמים show they do not, because metal carries heat along its whole length while wood does not. So the metal inside the animal does get hot and cooks the meat, and that is why our משנה forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) said to him, introducing a response

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows the חכמים: a metal spit carries heat inside the animal and cooks the meat, so it is not allowed for the פסח. A wooden spit does not carry heat.

phrases.english: They said to him:
This one (metal): when part of it is hot, all of it is hot,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה חַם מִקְצָתוֹ — אֵינוֹ חַם כּוּלּוֹ.
phrases.english: and that one (wood): when part of it is hot, not all of it is hot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: זֶה חַם מִקְצָתוֹ — חַם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים respond directly to רבי יהודה's comparison and break it apart.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יהודה's comparison between a wooden spit and a metal spit.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Metal carries heat through its whole length, but wood does not. So the two cannot be compared.

steps.title: Two nicknames for the roasted פסח lamb
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the משנה about placing the legs and innards inside the animal, a ברייתא gives two nicknames. רבי ישמעאל calls it 'תוך תוך' and רבי טרפון calls it 'גדי מקולס'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one places its legs, etc.' It was taught: רבי ישמעאל calls it 'תוך תוך'. רבי טרפון calls it 'גדי מקולס'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about where to put the legs and innards while roasting. It quotes a ברייתא with two nicknames for the roasted lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה brought a debate: put the legs and innards inside the lamb, or hang them outside so it does not look like cooking. רבי ישמעאל's name 'תוך תוך' fits the method of placing them inside the body, perhaps after the bubbling sound they make there. רבי טרפון's name 'גדי מקולס', a 'helmeted kid', fits innards hung on the spit above the animal's head like a helmet.

keyTerms.meaning: Calls it, gives it a name
A nickname connected to placing the parts inside the lamb
A 'helmeted kid', meaning a kid roasted whole with its parts hanging on it

phrases.english: 'And one places its legs, etc.'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, introducing the next topic.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yishmael calls it 'Tokh tokh'.
Rabbi Tarfon calls it 'a helmeted kid'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The roasted פסח had well-known nicknames: 'תוך תוך' (רבי ישמעאל) and 'גדי מקולס' (רבי טרפון).

steps.title: What kind of roasted kid is forbidden on פסח night today
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines the גדי מקולס that may not be eaten on פסח night today: an animal roasted whole all at once. If one limb was cut off or boiled, it no longer counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Which is the 'helmeted kid' that is forbidden to eat on פסח nights nowadays? Any animal that was roasted whole, all at once. If one limb was cut off it, or one limb was boiled, it is not a 'helmeted kid'.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the term גדי מקולס from the last step, a ברייתא gives a practical rule for today. It explains which roasted meat is forbidden on the night of פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no בית המקדש, we may not eat meat on פסח night that looks just like the קרבן פסח. Otherwise it might look as if we brought the קרבן outside the מקדש. The forbidden case is a kid roasted whole, like the פסח was. Changing it even slightly, by cutting off or boiling one limb, removes the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Nowadays, in a time without the בית המקדש
Roasted it whole, all at once

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about the real קרבן פסח. It is a rule for today, about ordinary meat that should not look like the קרבן פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the custom of not eating roasted whole meat at the סדר, and of changing the meat so it does not resemble the פסח.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Which is the 'helmeted kid'
that it is forbidden to eat on the nights of Passover
nowadays?
Any animal that one roasted whole, all at once!
If a limb was cut off from it,
or a limb of it was boiled,
this is not a 'helmeted kid'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the term גדי מקולס from the last step and gives a practical rule built on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nowadays it is forbidden on פסח night to eat a kid roasted whole. If even one limb was cut off or boiled, it is allowed.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא need to mention a boiled limb?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא mentions a boiled limb at all. If a limb that was only cut off, and still roasted with the animal, already removes the problem, then a cut-off limb that was boiled obviously does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, it says that if a limb was cut off, even though it is roasted together with the animal, you say it is not a גדי מקולס. Is it even necessary to say a boiled limb is not?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. It says the second case, the boiled limb, seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes a limb is boiled only after it has been cut off. If cutting it off is enough, even when it is still roasted, then cutting it off and also boiling it surely is. So why would the ברייתא bother to teach the boiled case?

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if already... (introduces a 'how much more so' argument)
Is it necessary? (meaning it is obvious)

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא יֵשׁ לוֹמַר נֶחְתַּךְ מִמֶּנּוּ אֵבֶר,
phrases.english: Now, one can say that if a limb was cut off from it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָא מִטְּוֵי לֵיהּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ,
phrases.english: that even though one roasts it together with the animal,
you said it is not a 'helmeted kid',
is it necessary to say so for a boiled limb?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא יֵשׁ לוֹמַר נֶחְתַּךְ מִמֶּנּוּ אֵבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in the last step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's second case, 'a limb was boiled'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a cut-off limb that is still roasted already removes the גדי מקולס problem, then a cut-off limb that was also boiled surely does. So the boiled case adds nothing.

steps.title: רב ששת: the limb was boiled while still attached
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the ברייתא means the limb was boiled while still attached to the animal. That is a new case, because nothing was ever cut off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is a case where he boiled the limb while it was still attached.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question by showing that the boiled case is a separate situation, not just a stronger version of the cut-off case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the boiled limb had been cut off first. רב ששת says the animal stayed whole and one attached limb was boiled. This teaches something new: even if the animal is still whole, cooking one limb in a different way stops it from being a גדי מקולס.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question

steps.whatToRemember: A גדי מקולס is a kid roasted completely whole, like the פסח. Either cutting off a limb, or boiling a limb while it is still attached, takes it out of that category, so it may be eaten on פסח night today.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It is where he boiled it while it was still attached.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by redefining the case of the boiled limb.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the boiled limb was never cut off.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the boiled limb had first been cut off, which would make the case obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limb was boiled while attached. This teaches that even a whole animal is not a גדי מקולס if one limb was boiled.

steps.title: רבה permits roasting meat stuffed inside an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that a מוליתא, raw meat stuffed inside an animal being roasted, is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: This stuffing of meat inside a roasting animal is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the משנה to a general question about blood. רבה says you may roast an animal stuffed with raw meat, even though the stuffing was never salted to remove its blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, blood in meat must be removed before eating, by salting or by roasting over fire. The worry is that blood leaving the stuffing could soak into the outer animal. רבה says this is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Stuffing: raw meat placed inside another animal that is being roasted
An אמורא who gives the ruling here

phrases.english: Rabba said:
This stuffing (of raw meat inside a roasting animal) is permitted.
phrases.notes: The stuffed meat was not salted, so its blood is still inside it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about absorbing blood. It is connected to the משנה's case of placing innards inside the קרבן פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roasting an animal stuffed with unsalted raw meat is permitted.

steps.title: אביי objects that the outer meat absorbs blood
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: the roasting animal soaks up blood released by the stuffing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But it absorbs blood!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's ruling. As the stuffing heats up, its blood comes out and soaks into the outer animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is practical. Releasing blood from the stuffing is not enough if that blood just moves into the meat around it. Then the outer meat would contain forbidden blood.

keyTerms.meaning: But behold, a formula that opens a challenge

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But it (the outer animal) absorbs blood (from the stuffing)!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא קָא בָּלַע דְּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבה's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that מוליתא is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The blood that leaves the stuffing gets absorbed into the outer meat, so that meat should become forbidden.

steps.title: As it absorbs, so it releases
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the outer meat releases the blood in the same way that it absorbed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As it absorbs it, so it releases it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his ruling. The same fire that pushes blood into the outer meat also pulls that blood back out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה agrees that blood is absorbed, but he says it does not stay there. The roasting continues, so the absorbed blood drips out again. In the end, no blood remains in the outer meat.

keyTerms.meaning: As it absorbs it, so it releases it: the absorbed blood comes back out through the same process

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle כבולעו כך פולטו is a basic rule in the laws of absorption (בליעות) and of making vessels kosher (הגעלה) throughout הלכה.

phrases.english: He (Rabba) said to him:
As it absorbs it, so it releases it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts that blood is absorbed, but explains that it is released again
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The blood absorbed into the outer meat stays there and makes the meat forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fire draws the absorbed blood back out, so the outer meat stays permitted.

steps.title: Trying to support רבה from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה, which allows placing the legs and innards inside the קרבן פסח, supports רבה because it relies on כבולעו כך פולטו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: 'He places its legs and its innards inside it.' What is the reason? Is it not because we say: as it absorbs, so it releases?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to bring a proof for רבה from our own משנה. There, the legs and innards are roasted inside the קרבן פסח, just like a stuffing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Legs and innards still have blood in them, and the קרבן פסח would absorb that blood. The משנה allows it anyway. The suggestion is that the only reason must be כבולעו כך פולטו, which is exactly רבה's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it supports him: a formula that opens a suggested proof

phrases.english: Let us say (the משנה) supports him:
He places its legs
and its innards inside it.
What is the reason?
Is it not because we say
as it absorbs it, so it releases it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for support from the משנה for רבה's principle.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that stuffed meat is permitted because of כבולעו כך פולטו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: נותן את כרעיו ואת בני מעיו לתוכו

steps.title: The קרבן פסח is different because of the open slaughter cut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The קרבן פסח has an open, hollow slaughter cut, so its case is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: It is different there, since there is the place of slaughter, which is hollow and open,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The case in the משנה may be special because the slaughtered animal has an open cut at the neck. This explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection claims that the משנה does not depend on כבולעו כך פולטו. The open slaughter cut seems to give the blood a way to drain out. A closed stuffed animal, like a מוליתא, would not have that, so the משנה cannot prove רבה's case.

keyTerms.meaning: They say: introduces an answer, often a rejection
The place of slaughter (the cut at the neck)
Hollow or open, with a passage through it

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished. The rest of the reasoning appears at the start of the next passage.

phrases.english: They say: It is different there,
since there is the place of slaughter, which is hollow (open),
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not reject רבה's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The קרבן פסח has an open slaughter cut, so the blood may drain out for that reason and not because of כבולעו כך פולטו.
